title: Recuay architectural vessel, 2020.222
place: Central Andes, Peru. Attributed to the Recuay people.
material: Ceramic with slip and resist painting
observation: The ceramic vessel gives a building and small figures three-dimensional form. The museum describes the building’s use and the gathering as interpretations.
limit: A modelled building on a vessel does not identify a particular house, family or event.
near: Tavi follows the reduced side view from the low rail. They ask for the facade and the figures to be described on separate lines.
wide: Jase waits behind the wide rail, then uses the full-span drawing to distinguish the building edge from the figures. The drawing gives them a better angle on the vessel.

title: Paint box of Vizier Amenemope, 1914.680
place: Egypt, Dynasty 18. The inscription names the vizier Amenemope.
material: Boxwood with an inscription inlaid in Egyptian blue
observation: The box holds five colour pots. The museum reports that conservators identified pigments using X-ray diffraction.
limit: The coloured inlay and pigment pots are different parts of the record. Their measured width does not reveal who painted with the box.
near: Tavi reads the short traced compartments at the low rail. They request the inscription as a separate line because the reduced scale hides fine strokes.
wide: Jase follows the full-span compartment trace at the wide rail. They record the length next to the scale and give the material line a separate place.

title: Akan-style geometric gold weight, 1962.244
place: Present-day Ghana. The museum attributes it to an Akan-style artist.
observation: The catalogue groups this small casting with weights used in weighing gold. It identifies the material of the casting as copper alloy.
limit: The dimensions do not give the object’s mass or prove a unit of trade for this specimen.
near: Tavi can go close enough to see the profile at its measured size. They keep the metal separate from the material the instrument was used to weigh.
wide: Jase asks for the close view beside the wide rail. A full-size outline alone is too small to resolve from the usual waiting place.

title: Hawaiian tapa cloth beater, 1971.152
place: Hawai‘i, Polynesia. The museum lists no named maker.
edge: catalogued length, with other dimensions open
observation: The museum describes a wooden beater with four sides for different stages of smoothing bark cloth.
limit: The catalogue’s single dimension cannot establish the thickness, balance or full grip of this particular tool.
near: Tavi uses the reduced length guide and reads the four sides from the label. They leave space on their own slip for dimensions the museum does not give.
wide: Jase walks the full-length guide from end to end. They ask to keep the length marked on one edge and the four faces on another.

title: Feline incense burner from Khurasan, 1948.308
place: Khurasan, Iran, attributed to the Seljuq period by the museum.
material: Cast, engraved, chased and pierced copper alloy
observation: The head was cast separately and can be removed. The museum describes the animal as possibly a caracal.
limit: The height leaves the exact animal identification and the object’s individual occasions of use open.
near: Tavi sees the whole reduced silhouette at the low rail. They keep the separately made head marked in the illustration key.
wide: Jase reads the full-span drawing, then turns to the photograph for the meeting of head and body. They leave the species tentative in the catalogue note.
